_comment: FIELD PRESENCE, measured against the live pools. This is SHAPE ONLY: field names and
how many documents carry each. No prose, no picks, no addresses.
WHAT IT IS FOR. tools-undefined-sweep.js uses it to tell a field that is ALWAYS
present from one that is SOMETIMES ABSENT. An unguarded read of an always-present
field is noise; an unguarded read of a sometimes-absent one is the defect that put
'The read undefined' on five stage cards and 'undefined' down 15 rows of the Note
column. The difference is not visible in the source, only in the data, which is why
a grep could never have found either.
ONE FIXTURE PER POOL, AND THE BOARD DECIDES WHICH ONE. Measuring the Tour board
against the Vuelta's data produced a confident wrong answer on 2026-09-13: the Vuelta
carries raceRow.extra on 6 of 21 rows and the TOUR CARRIES IT ON ALL 21, so the
${r.extra} that really was printing 'undefined' fifteen times on the Vuelta cannot
currently print it once on the Tour. Same code, different data, opposite verdict.
A fixture describes the data at the READ SITE, and which pool a board reads is part
of that.
REGENERATE from a signed-in owner board tab whenever the document shape changes, and
certainly when a new race starts. A stale fixture makes the gate weaker, not wrong:
it can only miss a newly-optional field, never invent one.
counts under `optional` are present/total.

boards._comment: built file -> which pool's data it renders

stage._source: pools/vuelta-2026/stages/*, AS THE BOARD SEES IT after buildCDF
_normalized: THE FIXTURE DESCRIBES CDF.stages, NOT THE RAW FIRESTORE DOCUMENT. buildCDF does
Object.assign({n:Number(d.id)}, v), so `n` is supplied from the document id
whenever the document lacks it. Raw stage docs 1, 2 and 3 genuinely have no `n`,
and an audit reading Firestore directly sees three undefineds collapse into one
null key. The BOARD never sees that. So `n` is listed under always, on purpose:
measuring the raw documents instead produced eleven false failures against render

stage._source: pools/col-du-fantasy/stages/*, with n supplied the way buildCDF does

_note: extra is on ALL 21 rows here, which is why the Tour board's unguarded
${r.extra} is not currently a live defect even though it is the same code
that printed the word fifteen times on the Vuelta. It is guarded anyway:
the row that loses its extra is the one that would print it.

_comment: Which board identifiers hold documents of which collection. A callback parameter
is bound by the sweep from patterns like RACE.map(r=>...), so this only needs the
COLLECTION identifiers, not every local name. Shared across pools: the two boards
are the same code and use the same names.
